wu: Predict the Weather: Students stand in a circle. Teacher shows a flashcard (sun, rain, snow) and asks 'What will the weather be like tomorrow?' Students reply 'It will be sunny/rainy/snowy.'
wuAlt: Future Timeline: Draw a line on the board from 2024 to 2035. Students write one prediction for each year.
Prediction Pictionary: Teacher draws a simple future event (e.g., flying car), students guess 'You will fly to school.'
pres: Show a news clip about AI in Morocco. Model sentences: 'AI will probably help doctors.' 'Robots won't replace teachers.' 'Self-driving cars are likely to arrive by 2030.' Check understanding with thumbs up/down for true/false predictions.
presAlt: Future Jobs Poster: Display jobs (doctor, farmer, influencer). Ask 'Will this job exist in 2040?' Students use 'probably/likely to'.
Morocco 2050 Video: Play a silent clip of futuristic Oujda. Students predict using 'will/won't'.
prac: Prediction Relay: Teams race to write sentences on the board about Moroccan festivals (e.g., 'Next Green March, drones will fly over the city.'). Correct spelling/grammar earns points.
pracAlt: Probability Dice: Roll a die (1=won't, 2-3=maybe, 4-5=probably, 6=will). Students make predictions about school life (e.g., 'We will have more exams.').
Find Someone Who...: Walk around asking 'Will you...?' questions (e.g., 'Will you travel abroad next year?').
ls: Listen to a podcast about future tech in Africa. Students tick predictions heard: 'Solar panels will power homes.' 'People won't use cash.'
re: Future Charades: Act out a future action (e.g., 'flying to Casablanca'). Class guesses 'You will travel by plane!'
prod: 2035 Morocco Project: Groups create a poster with 5 predictions about life in Morocco (e.g., 'Electric cars will be common.'). Justify each with 'because...'. Present to class.
rw: Read a short article about AI in Moroccan schools. Underline all uses of 'likely to'. Then write 3 predictions about your own school using 'will/won't'.
st: Read 'The Boy Who Predicted the Future' story (about a boy predicting Morocco's first satellite launch). End with: 'Today we learned to make predictions. Thank you, class!'
g: Pass a ball and say a prediction about the next student (e.g., 'You will answer a question well.')
Write 9 predictions in a grid. Cross off when a classmate admits it's true.
Start with 'Maybe I will...' and each student adds one prediction to the chain.
Students brainstorm 3 things that definitely won't happen by 2030 (e.g., 'Camels won't drive cars.')
Show scenarios (e.g., 'Morocco wins the World Cup'). Students hold up 'likely' or 'not likely' cards.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 50-word story about a future day in Oujda using 5 'will' predictions.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'I think... will...' and 'It will probably... because...'.
hw: Record a 1-minute video predicting your life in 2035 (e.g., 'I will be a doctor.').
Write 5 predictions about a famous Moroccan person (e.g., 'Ronaldo will visit Morocco.').
Interview a family member about their future predictions and write 3 sentences.
tip: Use local context (e.g., 'Will the new high-speed train change travel?') to make predictions relevant. Teens engage more when discussing their own future in Morocco.
